key_insight: SpanVLA combines autoregressive language reasoning with a flow-matching action expert and a span-based action bridge, enabling low-latency, robust action generation by training on both standard and negative-recovery trajectories.
problem_solved: Reduces high latency and limited robustness of autoregressive-only Vision-Language-Action (VLA) models, improving real-time control and handling of long-tail/failure scenarios in autonomous driving.
method: Hybrid pipeline: keep autoregressive reasoning for high-level planning, then pass compact span outputs to a flow-matching action expert for fast continuous action synthesis.
Span-based action bridging: translate discrete language/planning spans into grounded action primitives to align reasoning and control domains.
Negative-recovery training: augment training with failure (negative) samples and explicit recovery trajectories to improve robustness and generalization in long-tail situations.
impact: Enables practical, real-time VLA deployment by cutting action-generation latency while increasing resilience to rare/failure cases—useful for researchers and engineers building multimodal control systems.
visual_elements: Architecture diagram: left-to-right pipeline showing Autoregressive Reasoning → Span Bridge → Flow-Matching Action Expert with dataflow arrows.
Latency vs. Robustness chart: compare autoregressive-only baseline and SpanVLA (lower latency, higher recovery rate) across normal and long-tail scenarios.
Trajectory visualization: example negative (failure) state and the recovered trajectory generated by SpanVLA overlaid on a driving scene.
Icon set: language/brain icon for reasoning, link/span icon for bridging, steering wheel/control for action expert, and clock/shield for latency & robustness.
paper_title: SpanVLA: Efficient Action Bridging and Learning from Negative-Recovery Samples for Vision-Language-Action Model
paper_authors: Zewei Zhou, Ruining Yang, Xuewei, Qi, Yiluan Guo
